title: Teaching in the Church
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Teaching in the church is the faithful instruction of God’s people in sound doctrine, Scripture, and obedience to Christ. Teaching forms disciples by helping believers understand and live the truth.
summary: Teaching in the church is the faithful instruction of God’s people in sound doctrine, Scripture, and obedience to Christ. Teaching forms disciples by helping believers understand and live the truth.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Master Teacher and the content of faithful teaching. The church teaches so people may know Him, trust Him, obey Him, and grow into maturity in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The church is a teaching people because Christ commanded His disciples to teach all that He commanded. Doctrine is not optional decoration; it is necessary for faithful discipleship.

Teaching must be sound. Scripture commands teachers to speak what accords with sound doctrine, train faithful people, and equip the saints for maturity and service.

Teaching should aim at obedience, not information alone. The goal is not merely Bible knowledge, but lives shaped by truth, love, holiness, worship, and mission.

Teaching is also protective. Mature instruction helps believers avoid being tossed around by false teaching, emotional pressure, and the schemes of error.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
A church without sound teaching becomes vulnerable to confusion and immaturity. People may be sincere but unstable if they are not rooted in Scripture and doctrine.

This doctrine also dignifies patient, ordinary instruction. Sunday school, discipleship, family teaching, mentoring, and repeated explanation are not small things. God uses teaching to form His people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive teaching with humility and hunger for truth. Seek to grow beyond shallow understanding, and help others learn what Christ commanded. If you teach, do so faithfully, patiently, and with the aim of forming obedient disciples rather than impressing hearers.
